To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
screw dislocations play a key role in the oxidation of metals and the formation of non-planary oxide scales.

(i) the growth of oxide scale on metals and alloys occurs by the migration of screw dislocations at the metal/oxide interface, and (ii) the oxidation of pure copper and iron, nickel and cobalt, and chromium and iron alloys occurs via the same mechanism.
